catalog.chatSectionHint: measured on real localisation runs — pick one as your model
catalog.generalUse: Translates your strings and checks its own work
catalog.slotsFootnote: One model does everything here — it loads automatically on the first run; Load now just skips that first wait.

quickSetup.bandSub: A free local translation engine in one click — the models offered here are the ones MEASURED on real localisation runs, sized to this PC.
quickSetup.headSub: A free local translation engine in one click — measured models, sized to this PC.
quickSetup.modelHint: Pick a model — best first: every one here was measured on real localisation runs rather than guessed at. One click installs the engine if it's missing, downloads the model, loads it, and makes it the model the Translate & Confirm presets run on.
quickSetup.chatRole: translates your strings and checks its own work
quickSetup.doneBody: Translate and Confirm run on this model — change it any time under Routing by feature.

connectionError.need: read your locale files and run translations
connectionError.devHint: Dev: it should start automatically with `npm run dev`, or run it yourself with `npm run server`, then retry.
connectionError.portTaken: Another program is using port {port}. Close it, then press {retry}.
connectionError.portOtherUser: Another person signed in to this computer has the app open, on port {port}. One copy runs at a time: they can quit theirs (its tray icon), then press {retry}.
connectionError.portReserved: Windows has reserved port {port} for another use (Hyper-V, WSL or Docker), so the app can't use it. Restarting the computer usually frees it; Troubleshooting in the help says how to keep it free.
connectionError.serverError: Its server stopped as it started: {error}

intro.pointBody: at your en.json — the tool reads the locale folder and reports what it found.
intro.translateBody: locally and free with your own AI engine — or any online provider you connect.
intro.reviewBody: every finding, accept what's right, and ship translations you've actually seen.

home.translateHint: Missing + flagged keys for the ticked languages

runs.startHint: A run stages proposals — it NEVER writes your locale files. {pending} = missing + flagged (the dashboard's button) · {flagged} = every key the checks or the probe flagged · {unsure} = probe disagreements only · {all} = every key.
runs.exhausted: {n} key exhausted every retry: {keys} | {n} keys exhausted every retry: {keys}

docs.lede: Front-matter → locale keys. Author once, serve three surfaces.
docs.howBody: A help article's front-matter (title, lede, hints) is extracted into your locale files as ordinary keys — then the translate/review pipeline on this very dashboard carries them like any other string. One sentence, written once, translated once, shipped to the article, the surface lede and the field hint.
docs.runHint: The extractor is CLI-only for now — a UI runner is planned, and this page will grow it.

setup.lede: Point the tool at your app's i18n source file. Nothing here runs an engine.
setup.sourceHint: The path to your source locale file (usually en.json). Its folder is the locale folder and its name is the source language — one fact, nothing to disagree with.
setup.checkHint: Press {button} and the tool reports what it found — the part that catches a wrong path before an hour of engine time does.
setup.targetsHint: Which languages to translate into. Existing files are offered after a check, never pre-decided.
setup.contextHint: One sentence about the app — the one thing only you know.
setup.contextPlaceholder: e.g. JustWrite, a desktop app for writing novels
setup.glossaryHint: A term here is a BLANKET rule for every string. On a real project one wrong term turned 48 correct translations into findings — add only true brand and product names. A word that is a label in one string and prose in another belongs in review acceptances, not here.
setup.candidatesHint: Suggested from your strings (words recurring capitalised mid-sentence) — tick to add:
setup.gitignoreHint: Workshop files a re-run rebuilds. Your decisions (config, accepted, notes) stay committed.
setup.saveHint: Saving writes config.json into a just-ai-i18n-docgen folder at your app's root and loads it — no restart. Your reviewer name lives in {link}.

settings.title: Settings
settings.appearanceHint: Visual preferences, applied immediately and saved on this machine.
settings.backupsHint: The backup covers this tool's own data — connections, presets, models configuration, the reviewer name. Your locale files and accepted translations live in your project folder and travel with it (git keeps those safe).

storage.locationHint: One folder holds everything this tool saves — your connections, presets, the AI engine and models, and logs. Delete the folder, delete it all.
storage.moving: Moving your data — the app will restart…
storage.desktopOnly: Changing the folder is available in the desktop app.
storage.moveMessage: Everything this tool saves — connections, presets, the AI engine and models, and logs — moves to {folder}. The app restarts when the move finishes.
storage.diskHint: Where the data folder's space goes — and what can be reclaimed.
storage.clearModelsMessage: This frees {size} of downloaded model files. Your models stay in the catalog and re-download on demand.
storage.unloadFirst: A model is loaded — unload it first (AI page → Unload), then try again.

server.headlessHint: The server hosts the UI itself — {command} plus a browser gives the full app without the desktop shell.
server.keepRunning: Keep server running after the app closes
server.keepRunningHint: With this on, closing the window hides the app to the tray and the server keeps serving — use the tray to show the window again or quit for real.
server.tokensHint: Off by default. Add a token to require an {header} header on every {api} API call — for when you run the server exposed beyond this machine.
server.requireOnLocalhost: Require a token even on localhost

settings.logsHint: The live ring + per-day files. What the engine actually did, when.

reviewer.title: Reviewer
reviewer.hint: Your name, stamped on every acceptance — so a verdict can say who made it. Never taken from the OS. Tool-level: one name across every project.

about.blurb: Simple translation & help docs for your application — translated locally or online, verified, and reviewed by you.

why.spuriousInterrogative: the source is a statement, but the translation is a question
why.startpunc: this language opens questions and exclamations with a paired mark — one is missing or unpaired
why.endpunc: the source and the translation end with different punctuation
why.untranslated: the translation is identical to the English
why.placeholderChanged: an interpolation like {'{'}count{'}'} was lost, changed or duplicated
why.pluralHalvesLost: a plural form either side of {'|'} disappeared
why.pluralHalvesIdentical: the two halves either side of {'|'} are the same, so the plural does nothing
why.missing: this key has no translation at all
why.disagreement: a second pass worded this differently — the model was unsure here
why.terminology: this uses a different word than the rest of the catalogue does for the same term

review.emptySearch: Nothing here. Try another bucket, or clear the search.
review.emptyStaged: Nothing flagged — apply the staged translation above and the checks run on what gets written. | Nothing flagged — apply the {n} staged translations above and the checks run on what gets written.
review.emptyGreen: Nothing to review — the gate is green for {lang}.
review.noteSavedBody: It will be sent with this key on the next translation.
review.applyTitle: Apply {n} translation to {lang}? | Apply {n} translations to {lang}?
review.applyMessage: This writes {file} — the first time anything in this run touches your locale file. It is one Undo if it looks wrong.
review.appliedBody: One click, one Undo — the checks re-ran on what was written.
review.discardTitle: Discard {n} staged translation? | Discard {n} staged translations?
review.discardMessage: The run's output is thrown away. Your locale file is untouched — nothing was written yet — and re-running translates them again. One Undo brings the pile back.
review.discarded: {n} staged translation discarded | {n} staged translations discarded
review.readyNote: — staged by the last run; your {file} is untouched so far.
review.tickConfirmed: tick the {n} the engine calls correct
review.nothingAccepted: Nothing accepted yet for this language.
review.googleHint: An independent reading. Neither source is reliably better — on one measured key the local model was right and Google wrong; on another, the reverse. Copy it across only if you agree.
review.englishHint: Renders your translation back into English with the local model. Catches wrong words — not every defect, since an ambiguous source round-trips unchanged.
review.siblingsHint: The same namespace — how the pattern is rendered next door.
review.noteHint: Sent WITH this key next time it translates — how "Why:" stops coming back as "¿Por qué?". Fix it once, it stays fixed.
review.notePlaceholder: e.g. a label above a reasoning block, not a question
review.pickKey: Pick a key, or press j to start.
review.acceptedBody: Every entry names its check, pair of strings and reviewer. Un-accept puts a key back in the queue — a decision can always be revisited.

translate.hint: The batch translate loop — shield, send, restore, check.

review.label: Review
review.hint: Back-translation shown to the reviewer; never written to a catalogue.

confirm.label: Confirm
confirm.hint: The second opinion on byte-identical targets — annotates, never signs off.
